candidate_sentence_map.S1: Hepsor’s 2025 performance weakened compared with 2024, reflecting fewer apartment handovers, lower project margins and higher marketing costs.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Consolidated revenue declined 7.8% to €35.4 million from €38.4 million, while net profit fell 51.3% to €1.0 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Profit attributable to the parent’s owners was €0.4 million, broadly unchanged from €0.4 million in 2024, while profit attributable to non-controlling interests declined to €0.6 million from €1.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Gross profit decreased to €5.6 million from €6.8 million, and the gross margin narrowed to 15.9% from 17.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Operating profit fell to €3.4 million from €4.3 million, with the operating margin declining to 9.5% from 11.3%.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: EBITDA decreased to €3.5 million from €4.5 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Revenue fell to €4.5 million from €10.5 million, and the Group recorded a net loss of €0.5 million compared with a €1.0 million profit in the comparable quarter.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: The quarterly gross margin declined to 15.3% from 24.0%, while the net margin was -10.7%, compared with 9.1% in Q4 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: An €0.8 million gain from revaluing properties transferred to investment property supported fourth-quarter operating profit, which was €0.3 million versus €2.0 million a year earlier.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The main operating factor was the reduction in apartments handed over, to 141 from 194, including 22 in the fourth quarter compared with 52 previously.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: The gross margin on sold projects also declined to 16.9% from 17.8%, while marketing expenses rose to €1.3 million from €0.9 million because more projects were offered for sale and required greater sales activity.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Conversely, primary sales agreements increased substantially to 185 homes worth €36.1 million, compared with 109 homes worth €19.8 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Revenue generated in Latvia increased to €9.3 million from €5.9 million, partly offsetting the decline in Estonia, where revenue fell to €26.1 million from €32.5 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Active projects increased to 33 from 24, with sellable area rising to approximately 196,650 square metres from 172,500 square metres.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Homes under construction increased to 428 from 192, supported by four new project starts in Estonia and Latvia.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: The Group also expanded its Canadian portfolio and received building rights for the Weston Road project in Toronto.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: At year-end, total assets rose 3.4% to €91.8 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Interest-bearing liabilities declined to €47.7 million from €54.7 million, and the debt ratio improved to 52.0% from 61.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Equity increased 23.0% to €27.1 million, lifting the equity ratio to 29.5% from 24.8%.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: Cash decreased to €3.8 million from €6.2 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S23: In November, Hepsor raised €8.0 million through its first bond issue, carrying a fixed annual interest rate of 9.5%, strengthening funding for its expanded development programme.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1-K5, K7, and K8, with clear representation of revenue, profit, margin changes, apartment handovers, sales agreements, profitability pressures, bond issuance, and project expansion. However, K6 (portfolio expansion details including Manufaktuuri 3 site), K9 (2026 project launches), and K10 (February 2026 loan agreement) are entirely missing, representing significant omissions of HIGH-importance information that changes the overall understanding of the company's development pipeline and financing activities. While most key financial and operational metrics are present, these missing elements prevent full coverage.
